name: transcription

frames.best_why: The current word sits in a clear grey highlight with playback part way and the progress bar advanced.

tagline: Read-along transcript where the spoken word is boxed as playback runs.
summary: A podcast transcript tied to a running clock. The word being spoken is highlighted, words already spoken dim, and clicking any word jumps the playback to that moment.
appearance: A dark card with a round play button, an episode title and byline, a timecode and a hairline progress bar. Below, a paragraph of small grey words wraps over four lines, with the current word set in a grey box and past words dimmer than upcoming ones.
behaviour: The clock walks a highlight through the words, dimming those already spoken and paling those still ahead. Clicking a word seeks there, and the bar and timecode follow the same clock until the end.
demo_content: Product Notes, Ep. 42 with Priya Raman discussing a shortened onboarding screen.
search_phrases: transcript that highlights the spoken word
click a word to jump the audio
words light up as they play
use_when: A podcast or interview page should let people read along and click any word to replay it.
avoid_when: The demo lets words crowd together with almost no spacing, so long passages are hard to scan.
customise: Segments with text and start and end seconds come in as an array, plus a current time, a seek callback and your own per-word render function.
weight_why: A few dozen word buttons coloured by the current time; no timers inside it.

a11y.note: Every word is a button so seeking works from the keyboard, but the active word is never announced and there is no progress role.

issues: Several opening words sit jammed together with no space, so the first lines read as one string.
The current word's highlight box can spill across two words when one wraps, as in frame 4.
polish_why: Competent synced transcript, but the collapsed word spacing makes the paragraph read badly.
